newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul asks Australia to halt beef sales on anthrax.
newsitem.headline: Seoul asks Australia to halt beef sales on anthrax.

text.p: South Korea's Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry said on Thursday it has asked Australia to halt beef exports from areas hit by the disease anthrax and slaughtered after January 26.
The ministry said in a statment it had delivered the request to the Australian embassy in Seoul on Wednesday.
The ministry also ordered the state-run National Animal Quarantine Service to check imports of Australian beef for signs of anthrax.
"As of February 19, there have been no imports of Australian beef slaughtered after January 26," the ministry said.

The outbreak of cattle anthrax in the southern Australian state of Victoria appeared to be under control after a massive vaccination programme, a spokesman for the state's Department of Natural Resources and Environment said last Thursday.
Anthrax, a bacterial infection, causes rapid death in cattle, sheep and goats which eat contaminated material. It rarely affects humans but can be contracted through a small cut or scratch.
In January, South Korea imported 7,703 tonnes of Australian beef out of total imports of 19,000 tonnes, according to the quarantine office.
South Korea's beef imports totalled 147,000 tonnes in 1996, compared with 148,000 tonnes the previous year, the ministry said.
Australia supplied 32 percent of the total imports for the two years -- 48,000 tonnes in 1996 and 47,000 tonnes in 1995.
